newsitem.title: INDIA: India seeks bids for 1,000 megawatt thermal plant.
newsitem.headline: India seeks bids for 1,000 megawatt thermal plant.

text.p: India has floated a global tender for a 1,000-megawatt thermal power project at Nabinagar in the eastern state of Bihar, a Power Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The integrated power project includes development of a captive five million tonnes a year coal mine, under a build, own and operate system," a Power Ministry official told Reuters.
A mining block with estimated coal reserves of 268 million tonnes has been identified at Dumargarh in Bihar for the power plant, he said.

The global bids are being coordinated by state-run transmission company, Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. "The names of shortlisted bidders will be announced by the end of 1997," the official said.

Power Grid will transmit electricity from the plant to neighbouring states. About 80 percent of the power generated will be supplied to the northern region and the remainder transmitted to eastern region, the official said.
The firm that sets up the plant will be allowed to sell electricity to bulk consumers and state electricity boards. "But these will be separate power purchase agreements," he said.
"The central government is considering providing financial guarantee to comfort the successful bidder so that its revenue stream is maintained," the official said.
India faces a power crisis. It requires additional generation capacity of 57,735 megawatts during the Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002) to meet current demand trends.

In order to meet the electricity shortfall, the Power Ministry has allowed the private sector to set up projects of 1,000 megawatts and above. The projects are to be located near coalmines to ensure economies of scale.
